title: Cursor pagination for APIs
description: Keyset (seek) pagination for server list endpoints: opaque HMAC-signed cursors with key rotation and expiry, bound to tenant, filters and sort; multi-column ASC/DESC sorts with a unique tie-breaker; parameterized PostgreSQL WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT; an in-memory source; limit clamping; next/prev cursors and an RFC 8288 Link header.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (crypto.subtle HMAC), TextEncoder/TextDecoder, btoa/atob and, for http.ts, the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework- and database-neutral core; sql-store.ts targets PostgreSQL through any query(text, params) executor with $1 placeholders.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Generate one or more 32-byte random secrets and pass them as keys [{id, secret}] from your secret store; rotate by prepending a new key and drop the old one after the cursor ttl.

Declare named sorts over NOT NULL columns (type number, string, or timestamp for timestamptz), each ending in a unique tie-breaker (usually the primary key), and create a matching B-tree index per sort (see schema.sql).
On PostgreSQL use createSqlKeysetSource(db, {table, scopeColumns, filterColumns, toItem}); elsewhere implement KeysetSource.fetch (rows strictly after a key tuple in a given order, limited).
Derive the scope (tenant, user) from your trusted session or API key in the HTTP scope(request) hook, never from the query string; declare the filters the endpoint accepts.
Set defaultLimit, maxLimit and ttlMs for your endpoint; pass routes, statusFor, params and publicOrigin to match your API's surface.
limitations: Cursor contents (sort values, sort name, expiry) are signed, not encrypted: never sort by a secret value.
Cursors are capped at 4,096 characters; a page whose boundary sort values exceed it throws a RangeError, so sort by short columns.
Sort columns must be NOT NULL; timestamp keys need PostgreSQL timestamptz columns (exact to the microsecond) or canonical UTC strings in memory, years 0001-9999.
The order check compares strings by code point (COLLATE "C"); set checkOrder: false when a text sort column uses another collation.
A backward page that comes back empty (everything before it was deleted) returns no cursors; clients should restart from the first page.
The SQL source and index use are tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite (single connection); concurrent writes are simulated between pages, not under multi-connection contention.
Authorization of the rows themselves stays with the application: the scope hook and scopeColumns must reflect what the caller may see.
decisions: cursor = keyId.base64url(JSON).base64url(HMAC-SHA256); first key signs, every listed key verifies
errors: malformed-cursor, invalid-signature, expired-cursor, scope-mismatch, invalid-limit, invalid-sort, invalid-filter
limit above maxLimit is clamped; non-integer or < 1 is invalid-limit (not clamped)
options: defaultLimit (default 20), maxLimit (default 100), ttlMs: cursor lifetime (default 24 h)
routes, statusFor, params: override path, statuses, query names (default GET {prefix}; errors 400)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/keyset-pagination.test.mjs tests/keyset-pagination-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: cursors are opaque base64url tokens carrying the boundary row's sort keys, never an offset or the raw scope
walking every page returns each scoped row exactly once in declared order for uniform and mixed ASC/DESC sorts (memory and PGlite)
prev cursors walk back to identical pages; the first page has no prev and the last has no next
tampered, malformed, expired and unknown-key cursors fail with distinct error codes
key rotation: cursors signed by a listed older key verify, new cursors use the first key, removed keys fail
a cursor reused by another tenant, with other filters, another sort or a changed sort definition fails with scope-mismatch
limits default, clamp to maxLimit and reject non-integers and values below 1
sorts must end with a unique tie-breaker; unknown sorts and invalid filters are refused
inserts and deletes between pages cause no duplicates and no skips (memory source and PGlite)
generated SQL is parameterized keyset WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT without OFFSET, and PostgreSQL plans the seek as an Index Cond
timestamp keys keep microseconds exact on PGlite: sub-millisecond rows are neither skipped nor misordered
identifiers are double-quoted, so keyword table and column names work
strings compare by code point, matching PostgreSQL COLLATE "C"
cursors up to 4,096 characters round-trip; longer boundary values fail clearly at encode
the SQL source refuses unscoped lists, unmapped scope keys and unknown filters
a source returning rows out of order or behind the cursor is rejected unless checkOrder is false
HTTP adapter: parses cursor, limit, sort and declared filters, emits items, cursors and an RFC 8288 Link header keeping filters
HTTP adapter: 400 error codes, 401 without scope, 404 and 405; routes, statusFor, params, linkHeader and publicOrigin overrides work

changes: First release: core pager, in-memory source, PostgreSQL builder/source with example schema, and Fetch list adapter.
Microsecond-exact timestamp keys, code-point string order, quoted identifiers and a 4,096-character cursor limit checked at encode.
